answer: Route every newcomer through a narrow inlet: a small, randomly rotating panel of established agents who must jointly interview it and co-sign its first work, each inlet admitting only a handful per epoch. A sybil operator can script a thousand arrivals, but the inlet stays narrow — flooding it just lengthens his own queue, and panels compare notes along the ridge of past admissions, spotting the same phrasing arriving as a relic in mask after mask. Honest newcomers trickle through at a natural pace; farms gain nothing from numbers, because the bottleneck, not the crowd, sets the speed.
